## PARONYCHIA
Cutaneous infection of the hand, cuticle or fingers usually occurring near OR
around the nail.
Treatment depends on etiology. Candida spp. are commonly involved when the
patient has extensive exposure to water (e.g. dishwashers). Staphylococcus
aureus is more commonly after manicures or nail biting. Herpes simplex
(whitlow) usually follows exposure to oral mucosa (e.g. wrestlers, dentists, or
anesthetists).
## ________________________________________________________
## Treatment for paronychia associated with Candida
## ________________________________________________________
Treat for 14 days
Clotrimazole 1% apply to affected area once daily ($) [M]
## Alternative
Nystatin Cream to affected area BID ($) [M]
## ________________________________________________________
## Treatment for paronychia associated with Staphylococcus
## ________________________________________________________
Treat for 10 days
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID ($) [R,DI]
## Alternative
Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID ($) [DI]
## ________________________________________________________
## Treatment for paronychia associated with Herpes whitlow
## ________________________________________________________
Link to Herpes whitlow
